transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-08-07
Start time: 14:30 PDT
Duration: 46 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Jordan Patel (Redwood AE); Maya Torres (Redwood SE); Evan Brooks (Zenith CTO); Lina Park (ML Eng); Samir Gupta (Infra)

Auto Summary (auto gen, may be rough): Discussed Zenith's latency and throughput targets for chat and batch embedding workloads; Redwood options (hosted, dedicated, private) and tradeoffs; agreed to run hosted benchmarks and share sizing/cost guidance.

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Jordan, I'm the AE working with Zenith. With me is Maya, our systems SE. Evan, Lina, Samir, thanks for taking the time. Quick round robin?
[00:22] Evan: Yep, thanks Jordan. I'm Evan, CTO. We're evaluating options for serving our customer-facing chat assistant and high-volume embedding index jobs. Key thing for us is p95 latency for chat under concurrent load and predictable throughput for embeddings.
[00:38] Lina: hi all, Lina here. we'll be running the evaluation, we have a small cluster today and want to understand what to expect in hosted vs dedicated.
[00:47] Samir: Samir, infra. Interested in VPC/on-prem considerations, KMS integration, and how much network egress vs compute we need.
[00:56] Maya: Great, thanks. At a high level, can you share the p95 target and concurrency numbers you care about for the chat flow? streaming or non-streaming?
[01:12] Evan: Our goal is pretty aggressive - we want p95 on response complete (end-to-end streaming) to be below 600ms for short prompts (user messages ~20-40 tokens) under a concurrency of 30 active users for the chat endpoint. For embeddings we want throughput of ~200 req/s at 512-dim vectors, but batching is fine there.
[01:34] Jordan: Good, that's helpful. Just to clarify, you said 600ms p95 for streaming end-to-end - do you mean first-byte or final token?
[01:43] Evan: final token ideally, because UX needs entire response. But first-byte under 200ms would be nice so stream looks snappy.
[01:53] Maya: OK. For hosted, our streaming infra can hit sub-200ms first-byte on smaller models and typical token widths, but final token p95 depends on model size, prompt length, and concurrency. We often recommend either model variants or dedicated capacity for strict p95 SLOs at high concurrency.
[02:12] Lina: Can you outline what 'dedicated' looks like - how many GPUs, NVMe, etc? We have inference on A100s in-house but capacity is not elastic.
[02:25] Jordan: Dedicated is reserved GPU pools in our data centers per customer. Typically we size based on target tokens/sec and concurrency. For chat with 30 concurrent users and average output length ~60 tokens, ballpark CPU/GPU mapping is X - (note: AE said exact numbers will be in sizing guide). We'll share a dedicated sizing worksheet.
[02:46] Samir: Any ballpark of tokens/sec per GPU? Our infra team needs a number to compare to our A100 usage.
[02:55] Maya: Sure - rough rule: depending on quantization and model family, you might see 150-450 tokens/sec per GPU for medium-sized models when optimized and with batching. For larger models (chat-optimized 7B-13B), expect lower tokens/sec. NVMe sharding and kernel selection matter too. These are approximate - we'll provide benchmarks.
[03:15] Evan: That spread is big. For our UX, the key is p95 not median. How do you measure p95? Is it from our app to your response?
[03:24] Maya: We profile at the token level inside the runtime - so we can report first-byte latency, per-token generation rates, and total response time. For hosted tests we can run end-to-end with your sample prompts to capture network variance. Note transcription: sometimes line said 'k v chase' when speaking about KV cache.
[03:44] Jordan: Also worth noting our smart routing and fallback. If you want strict SLOs we can provision Dedicated; Hosted with an elevated SLA and dedicated-like options is possible but depends on commit.
[03:55] Lina: For embeddings we do large batch jobs overnight; throughput matters more than latency there. Do you support continuous batching and auto-batching?
[04:06] Maya: Yes - automatic batching for embeddings and trickle batching for chat is standard. For embeddings we can hit much higher throughput when we batch across requests - we'll show a benchmark sheet where we run 512-dim embeddings at various batch sizes.
[04:20] Evan: Security is also critical. We need KMS integration and audit logs. Can hosted satisfy our compliance requirements or would Private be necessary?
[04:30] Maya: Hosted is SOC2 compliant, offers encryption at rest with customer-managed keys via KMS integrations in certain tiers; Private gives you full control - VPC peering and optional on-prem. We'll send SOC2 and KMS docs. For audits, dedicated and private provide more detailed audit trail options.
[04:47] Samir: On-networking for Private - do you support VPC endpoints and customer-managed gateways? We need to keep traffic on private links.
[04:56] Jordan: Yes, Private supports VPC and on-prem options, with peering and direct connect. We'll go over specifics in the follow-up deep-dive.
[05:05] (Background cross-talk)
[05:12] Evan: Can you run a hosted benchmark using our sample prompts? We prefer starting on hosted to avoid up-front infra changes.
[05:20] Maya: Totally. For hosted benchmarking we typically ask for a sample prompt set (about 200 prompts across short/medium/long), a representative concurrency profile, and expected token lengths. We'll spin up a run that records first-byte, per-token, and final p95 under simulated concurrency.
[05:38] Lina: What's a realistic time to get hosted benchmarks back?
[05:42] Maya: Usually 48-72 hours after we get the prompts and traffic patterns; may take longer if we need custom model variants. Jordan will coordinate.
[05:50] Jordan: I'll drop the sizing guide and a link to the benchmark template. Also I'll include pricing bands for hosted vs dedicated vs private baseline.
[05:59] Evan: On pricing, are you including burst capacity? We have spike periods where concurrency doubles for short windows.
[06:07] Maya: We support burst capacity on Dedicated and Hosted under certain commit levels. For Hosted bursts we also have throttles; Dedicated can be configured with reserved base plus burstable pool. We'll include options in the doc.
[06:19] Samir: Regarding quantization - do you recommend nf4, int8, or fp16 for our workloads? We saw quality regressions last time with int8 on some models.
[06:30] Maya: We typically recommend nf4 for mixed workloads as a good balance; int8 can be used when quality tradeoffs are acceptable. We'll run a small eval comparing model quality vs quantization and include the metrics. Also note: kernel choices and compilation can affect throughput.
[06:46] Lina: For the chat case, is streaming enabled by default? We want to do partial responses to the user while tokens are generated.
[06:54] Jordan: Yes, streaming is supported in all deployment modes - we just need to instrument it in the client and ensure the model and runtime produce low-latency first bytes.
[07:03] Evan: If final p95 at concurrency 30 is the measure, what would you recommend - Hosted with x commit or Dedicated sizing?
[07:12] Maya: Short answer: if you need strict 600ms final p95 at 30 concurrent users for ~60-token outputs, Dedicated is safer because you control packing, NVMe, and reserved capacity. Hosted can hit that in many cases but has more variance depending on noisy neighbors and multi-tenant routing. We can attempt hosted benchmark first and if it misses SLOs recommend Dedicated sizing.
[07:36] Jordan: We'll document tradeoffs. Maya will own the benchmark plan; I'll own pricing and commercial terms.
[07:44] Evan: Great. A few nitty-gritty items: can you measure p95 excluding network to isolate compute? Also show p95 including app-to-app so we understand total end-to-end.
[07:55] Maya: Yes, we can run both: instrument the runtime for compute-only, and run end-to-end tests from your client in your environment for network-included numbers. For Private we can do bare-metal-type measurements.
[08:10] Lina: Also can we set concurrency limits per route to shape latency?
[08:15] Maya: Absolutely - per-route concurrency and queueing policies are configurable. You can set max in-flight requests and automatic fallback policies.
[08:24] Samir: For the embedding overnight jobs, we might want to run on Dedicated spot instances if cost matters. Do you offer spot or preemptible capacity?
[08:33] Jordan: Yes, we have pricing options that include spot/dynamic pools for batch workloads to reduce cost; we'll include details.
[08:40] Evan: Any success stories for similar scale customers?
[08:43] Jordan: We have a few fintech and adtech customers who run high-concurrency chat and embeddings - we'll anonymize the numbers but share ranges in the sizing doc.
[08:52] (Pause)
[08:58] Lina: A minor note: when you said 'Redwood-Opt' earlier, did you mean Redwood Optimized runtimes?
[09:04] Maya: Yes, apologies - sometimes the auto-transcripts read odd. We have an optimized runtime and a general one; the optimized one includes kernel selection, attention ops, and quantization-friendly paths.
[09:17] Evan: OK, next steps recap?
[09:20] Jordan: Recap: 1) Jordan will send dedicated sizing guide, pricing bands, and SOC2/KMS docs. 2) Maya will prepare benchmark harness, sample prompts (200), and run hosted benchmark when Zenith provides prompts and traffic profile. 3) Schedule technical deep-dive on Private with Samir - 60 minutes. 4) Zenith to send traffic trace and explicit p95 targets.
[09:44] Samir: Sounds good. Let's target the deep dive for next week if possible.
[09:49] Jordan: I'll send calendar invites after this call.
[09:52] Evan: Thanks everyone. Appreciate the clarity.
[09:55] Jordan: Thanks all, we'll follow up with artifacts.

References / links mentioned: benchmark template (internal): https://redwood.ai/benchmarks/template (note: placeholder); Dedicated sizing worksheet: https://redwood.ai/sizing/dedicated (placeholder); SOC2 docs and KMS integration guide will be attached to the follow-up email.
